A. Roll Call
a. A meeting was held at 7:15 pm in Community Room A located in the City Hall Lobby.
b. Commissioner Brett C.S. Roberts, District 3, served as the interim chairperson for this meeting.
c. Commissioner Roberts introduced the new District 1 Commissioner to the panel
d. Attendees included:
 Richard Galido, Commissioner District 1
 Kip Rudd, Commissioner District 2

 Diana Maximo, Operations Manager (LAZ Parking)

a. May 2023 Meeting Minutes
 Commissioner Brett C.S. Roberts made a motion to accept the meeting notes. Seconded by

a. An Oak Street resident questioned why not all the Parking and Traffic Commission panel
  members were present. Also, resident questioned the reason for not being on the agenda to
  terminate the District 5C Residential Parking Permit. The resident inquired about having the
  same entitlement as the other Residential Parking Permit Districts.

D. Unfinished Business
a. The Commission announced that Public Works mailed ballots to amend the City's Parking Permit
  Program on 3rd Avenue from 90th Street to Manchester Blvd on District 7B in June 5, 2023. The
  deadline for residents to submit ballots to Public Works Department has been reported to be July
  6, 2023

E. New Business NONE

F. Public Hearing
a. To amend the Citywide Parking Permit Program at 5th Ave from 104th St to 108th St
 On the date of the meeting, the following comments were given as to why the resident does or
  does not support the parking program:
  1. Residents rely heavily on street parking.
  2. There are not enough driveways on the block where residents can use to park.
  3. The extended family lives in a house where the family owns more than four vehicles in a
  house.
  4. The program is inconvenient and unreasonable, not feasible to implement.

   PUBLIC RULES OF DECORUM
In compliance with the Ralph M. Brown Act and to further facilitate feedback, public comment is
encouraged at meetings of the City Council, its Authorities, Agencies, and Boards and Commissions, and
Committees and its Agencies, in accordance with the following rules. Please note Members of the
public are encouraged to contact the City Manager, or respective Operating Department Directors, first
before making service requests or service complaints directly to the Council.

    At the beginning of each meeting to consider Closed Session items, public comments are
  permitted to address one (1) or more Closed Session Items scheduled on the Agenda prior to the
  Inglewood City Council convening deliberations in private. Public comments during Closed
  Session shall not exceed a total of one (1) minute in length.

    At the beginning of each meeting to consider Open Session items (Consent Calendar, Warrants
  and Bills, Setting Public Hearings, Departmental Reports, Authority and Agency Items, Council
  Initiatives, etc.), public comments are permitted to address one (1) or more Open Session Items
  (excluding Closed Session Items, and Public Hearings) scheduled on the Agenda. Public
  Comments occurring at the beginning of Open Session shall not exceed a total of three (3)
  minutes in length.

    Public comments are not permitted on any scheduled Closed or Open Agenda item or Public
  Hearing in the event the item has been pulled from the Agenda, postponed or rescheduled for
  another date.

    Public comments to address a Public Hearing scheduled on the Agenda shall not to exceed 1
  minute in length.

    At the conclusion of the City Council meeting prior to adjournment, public comments are
  permitted on any items of interest to the public and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the
  City Council. Public comments occurring at the end of Open Session shall not to exceed one (1)
  minute in length.

    The Mayor, or Presiding Officer of the meeting may, at his or her discretion, restrict or grant
  additional speaker time based on such considerations as Agenda length, volume of speakers,
  complexity of item, or looming threat of loss of quorum.

    The Mayor, or Presiding Officer of the meeting may request that a spokesperson be chosen by
  the group to address the Council when a group of persons wish to comment on the same
  subject matter.

    Speakers are not permitted to cede their time, or any portion thereof, to another speaker.

    The Mayor, or Presiding Officer of the meeting, may invoke the use of speaker cards at any time
  use of such cards is deemed necessary to facilitate the orderly process of permitting public
  comment.
   All public comments are to be directed to the Mayor, or the Presiding Officer, and not to any
  other member of the public or to any single Council, Authority, Agency, Board, Commission, or
  Committee Member unless in response to a question from that Member.

  Any person making a public comment who wishes to provide written or other materials to the
  Mayor and Council must first request permission to approach the dais. If and when permission is
  granted, materials shall be given to the Sergeant At Arms for distribution.

  Commenters must be civil and respectful when addressing the Mayor and Council Members,
  and making reference to others.

  No person attending a public meeting shall engage in disorderly or boisterous
  conduct—including but not limited to applause, whistling, feet stamping, booing or making any
  loud, threatening, profane, abusive, personal, impertinent or slanderous uttering or comments.
  No person is allowed to disturb, disrupt, or otherwise impede the orderly conduct of the
  meeting.

  Members of the audience and speakers shall not wear or display signs, placards, banners, hats,
  costumes or similar items at any time in the Council Chamber that obstruct the view of the
  legislative body or audience members, or which creates sufficient disruption to impede the
  orderly conduct of the meeting or to intimidate other attendees of the meetings.

  Persons making public comment should not routinely expect to receive answers to questions
  posed during their remarks. Unlike Town Hall, Neighborhood Block, and other meetings and
  gatherings more conducive to question and answer format, City Council Meetings are business
  meetings. In many cases staff will be available to take speaker questions and contact
  information and respond in a timely manner.

  ENFORCEMENT OF RULES AND DECORUM
  The Mayor, or Presiding Officer of the Council or Committee, with the assistance of the
  Sergeant-at-Arms or any law enforcement officer, shall be responsible for maintaining the order
  of the meeting and uniformly enforcing the Rules of Decorum.

  In the event that any person breaches the Rules of Decorum, the Mayor, or Presiding Officer,
  shall order the person to cease the offending conduct.

  If any person continues to breach the Rules of Decorum in a manner that disturbs, disrupts or
  otherwise impedes the orderly conduct of the meeting following an order from the Mayor, or
  Presiding Officer, to cease the offending conduct, the Mayor, or Presiding Officer, may order
  that person to leave the meeting.

  If any person refuses to leave the public meeting following an order to do so from the Mayor or
  Presiding Officer, that person may be escorted out of the meeting by any law enforcement
  officer present and may be subject to arrest for violation of the California Penal Code or
  Inglewood Municipal Code.

DATE:  August 23, 2023

TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission

FROM:  Peter Puglese PE, TE, City Traffic Engineer

SUBJECT: Request to Amend Residential Permit Parking District for 2nd Avenue
  between 102nd Street to 104th Street within District 9

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the Parking and Traffic Commission conduct a public hearing to
do the following:
1. Receive Public Comments regarding the termination of Residential Permit Parking
  Program for 2nd Avenue between 102nd Street to 104th Street, within District 9; and
2. Provide direction to the City Engineer on how to proceed

BACKGROUND:
In June 2020, the City Council adopted a Citywide Residential Permit Parking Program.
The program is enforced 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with two-hour parking Monday
through Sunday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. (Ordinance No. 20-09). The program was adopted to
protect residential communities more effectively and efficiently from non-resident vehicle
intrusion.

On November 3, 2022, Public Works (PW) Department received a petition requesting the
removal of Residential Permit Parking for 2nd Avenue between 102nd Street to 104th
Street. Nineteen (19) valid signatures (one signature per residential unit) were submitted
on the petition, resulting in seventy-three percent (73%) of all households on the block
signing the petition in favor of removing the permit parking restrictions.

On August 9, 2023, a notice was sent to all addresses within the petition boundary to
attend the August Traffic and Parking Commission meeting to express their views on the
matter.

DISCUSSION:
Residential Permit Parking Districts encourage residents to use their driveways to park
their vehicles, when available, so that those without driveways can park on the street.
Public Works staff requests the Parking and Traffic Commission provide instructions on
how to proceed with the request by either:
1. Approve the request to start the voting process; or
2. Deny the request to end the processing of the petition.

  NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
  Petition for Termination of Permit Parking in
  Residential Neighborhood
A petition has been submitted to the Inglewood Public Works Department requesting the termination of
residential permit parking within District 9 on 2nd Avenue between 102nd Street to 104th Street. Per
Sections 3-75 to 3-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code, this matter will be presented to the Inglewood
Parking and Traffic Commission at the time and place specified:

  Wednesday August 23rd, 2023 at 7:00 p.m.
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

This notice is being mailed to all addresses within the subject area. Any interested person may attend this
meeting and speak on this matter.

  Purpose of Public Hearing
The purpose of this public hearing is to give all residents of the subject area listed above an opportunity to
state their opinion of the subject matter.

The purpose of the Residential Permit Parking Program is to assure the availability to residents of some on-
street (curbside) parking spaces within a neighborhood where the patrons and/or employees of a nearby
commercial or industrial facility are otherwise using all available on-street parking spaces.

The Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission will therefore be considering if the availability of on-street
parking is severely impacted and if the termination of a residential permit parking within District 9 on 2nd
Avenue between 102nd Street to 104th Street would be warranted. If it is determined to be warranted,
ballots will be mailed to each household within the subject area.

If a Residential Permit Parking District is terminated, all residents and visitors in this neighborhood will not
be restricted from parking on the public streets at any time; including during special events. If you have any
questions regarding this matter, or wish to express an opinion but are unable to attend the public hearing,
please contact the Inglewood Public Works Department at (310) 412-5333.

  AVISO DE AUDIENCIA PÚBLICA
  Petición de Eliminación del Permiso de
  Estacionamiento en la Zona Residencial
Se ha presentado una petición al Departamento de Obras Públicas de Inglewood solicitando la cancelación
del permiso de estacionamiento residencial dentro del Distrito 9 en 2nd Avenue entre 102nd Street to 104th
Street. De acuerdo con las Secciones 3-75 a 3-79 del Código Municipal de Inglewood, este asunto se
presentará a la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico de Inglewood a la hora y lugar especificados:

  Miércoles 23 de Agosto de 2023 a las 7:00p.m.
  En la Sala Comunitaria A en el Primer Piso
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

Este aviso se envía por correo a todas las direcciones dentro del área de asunto. Cualquier persona
interesada puede asistir a esta reunión y hablar sobre este tema.

  Propósito de la Audiencia Pública
El propósito de esta audiencia pública es dar a todos los residentes del área mencionada anteriormente la
oportunidad de expresar su opinión sobre el tema.

El propósito del Programa de Permisos de Estacionamiento Residencial es garantizar la disponibilidad para
los residentes de algunos espacios de estacionamiento en la calle (bordillo) dentro de un vecindario donde
los clientes y/o empleados de una instalación comercial o industrial cercana utilizan todos los espacios de
estacionamiento disponibles en la calle.

La Comisión de Tráfico y Estacionamiento de Inglewood, por lo tanto, considerará si la disponibilidad de
estacionamiento en la calle se ve gravemente afectada y si se justificaría la terminación de un permiso de
estacionamiento residencial dentro del Distrito 9 en 2nd Avenue entre 102nd Street to 104th Street. Si se
determina que está justificado, las boletas se enviarán por correo a cada hogar dentro del área en cuestión.

Si se rescinde un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial, no todos los residentes y visitantes
de este vecindario tendrán restricciones para estacionar en las calles públicas en cualquier momento;
incluso durante eventos especiales. Si tiene alguna pregunta sobre este asunto o desea expresar una
opinión pero no puede asistir a la audiencia pública, comuníquese con el Departamento de Obras Públicas
de Inglewood al (310) 412-5333.

TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission

FROM:  Peter Puglese PE, TE, City Traffic Engineer

SUBJECT:  Request to Terminate Residential Permit Parking Program for 3rd Avenue
  from Manchester Boulevard to 90th Street within District 7B

RECOMMENDATION:
It is requested that the Parking and Traffic Commission review the information included in this
report and approve the resolution to terminate the Residential Permit Parking Program within
District 7B on 3rd Avenue from Manchester Boulevard to 90th Street.

BACKGROUND:
In June 2020, the City Council adopted a Residential Permit Parking Program. The program is
enforced 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with two-hour parking Monday through Sunday, 8 a.m.
to 5 p.m. (Ordinance No. 20-09). The program was adopted to protect residential communities
more effectively and efficiently from non-resident vehicle intrusion.

On September 28, 2022, Public Works (PW) Department received a petition requesting the
removal of Residential Permit Parking for 3rd Avenue from Manchester Boulevard to 88th Street.
A second petition was filed with the Department of PW on November 24, 2022 for 3rd Avenue
from 88th Street to 90th Street. The PW Department staff received and reviewed the
applications and combined them into one to be on 3rd Avenue from Manchester Boulevard to
90th Street. Seventeen (17) valid signatures (one signature per residential unit) were submitted
on the petition, resulting in forty-two percent (42%) of all households on the block signing the
petition in favor of removing the permit parking restrictions.

On May 9, 2023, a notice was sent to the resident inviting them to the May Parking and Traffic
Commission meeting to express their views on the matter. The notice was sent to all residents
of the petition along with a buffer zone of 300 feet from the area in question.

DISCUSSION:
On May 24, 2023, the Parking and Traffic Commission held a public hearing on the issue of
terminating the Residential Permit Parking Program for 3rd Avenue from Manchester Boulevard
to 90th Street within District 7B. The Public Works Department requested that the Parking and
Traffic Commission listen to public comments and provide direction on whether the petition
should go to a vote by the residents. As a result, all district commissioners voted to approve the
request to begin the voting process.

On June 5, 2023, the Public Works Department mailed questionaries to each resident residing
in the boundary area of the petition and requested the questionnaires be returned within thirty
(30) calendar days. July 6, 2023 was the deadline for the City to accept responses to the

of households supported the approval to terminate the Residential Permit Parking Program on

For the parking restrictions to be removed, a minimum of seventy-five percent (75%) of the
returned questionnaires must be in favor of the removal. Therefore, based on the results of the

resolution to terminate the Residential Permit Parking Program for 3rd Avenue from Manchester

  NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
  Petition for Elimination of Permit Parking in
  Residential Neighborhood
A petition has been submitted to the Inglewood Public Works Department requesting the termination of
Residential Permit Parking within District 7B at 3rd Avenue from 90th Street to Manchester Blvd. Per
Sections 3-75 to 3-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code, this matter will be presented to the Inglewood
Parking and Traffic Commission at the time and place specified:

  Wednesday May 24, 2023 at 7:00 p.m.
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

This notice is being mailed to all addresses fronting the subject street. Any interested person may attend
this meeting and speak on this matter.

  Purpose of Public Hearing
The purpose of this public hearing is to give all residents of the specific areas listed above an opportunity
to state their opinion of the subject matter.

The purpose of the Residential Permit Parking Program is to assure the availability to residents of some on-
street (curbside) parking spaces within a neighborhood where the patrons and/or employees of a nearby
commercial or industrial facility are otherwise using all available on-street parking spaces.

The Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission will therefore be considering if the availability of on-street
parking is severely impacted in this manner and if the termination of a Residential Permit Parking within
District 7B at 3rd Avenue from 90th Street to Manchester Blvd would be warranted. If it is determined to be
warranted, ballots will be mailed to each household within the proposed parking district. A seventy-five
percent (75 %), approval is required to eliminate a Residential Permit Parking District.

If a Residential Permit Parking District is eliminated, all residents and visitors in this neighborhood will not
be restricted from parking on the public streets at any time; including during special events. If you have any
questions regarding this matter, or wish to express an opinion but are unable to attend the public hearing,
please contact the Inglewood Public Works Department at (310) 412-5333.

Se ha presentado una petición al Departamento de Obras Públicas de Inglewood solicitando la cancelación
del Permiso de Estacionamiento Residencial dentro del Distrito 7B en 3rd Avenue entre 90th Street y
Manchester Blvd. De acuerdo con las Secciones 3-75 a 3-79 del Código Municipal de Inglewood, este
asunto se presentará a la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico de Inglewood a la hora y lugar
especificados:

  Miércoles 24 de Mayo de 2023 a las 7:00p.m.
  En la Sala Comunitaria A en el Primer Piso
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

Este aviso se envía por correo a todas las direcciones que se encuentran al frente de la calle en cuestión.
Cualquier persona interesada puede asistir a esta reunión y hablar sobre este tema.

  Propósito de la Audiencia Pública
El propósito de esta audiencia pública es brindar a todos los residentes de las áreas específicas
enumeradas anteriormente la oportunidad de expresar su opinión sobre el tema. El propósito del Programa
de Permisos de Estacionamiento Residencial es garantizar la disponibilidad para los residentes de algunos
espacios de estacionamiento en la calle (bordillo) dentro de un vecindario donde los clientes y/o empleados
de una instalación comercial o industrial cercana utilizan todos los espacios de estacionamiento disponibles
en la calle.

La Comisión de Tráfico y Estacionamiento de Inglewood, por lo tanto, considerará si la disponibilidad de
estacionamiento en la calle se ve gravemente afectada de esta manera y si se justificaría la terminación de
un Permiso de Estacionamiento Residencial dentro del Distrito 7B en 3rd Avenue entre 90th Street y
Manchester Blvd. Si se determina que está justificado, las boletas se enviarán por correo a cada hogar
dentro del distrito de estacionamiento propuesto. Se requiere una aprobación del setenta y cinco por ciento
(75 %) para eliminar un distrito de estacionamiento con permiso residencial.

Si se elimina un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial, no se restringirá el estacionamiento
en las calles públicas a todos los residentes y visitantes de este vecindario en ningún momento; incluso
durante los eventos especiales. Si tiene alguna pregunta sobre este asunto o desea expresar una opinión
pero no puede asistir a la audiencia pública, comuníquese con el Departamento de Obras Públicas de
Inglewood al (310) 412-5333.

The purpose of this letter is to allow residents the opportunity to vote on the removal of the
residential permit parking for 3rd Avenue from Manchester Boulevard to 90th Street within
District 7C. By voting "approve", this street will not be subject to the rules of a Residential
Permit Parking District. By voting "reject", this street will continue to have permitted parking
and follow the rules associated with it. The complete rules and procedures can be found in the
Inglewood Municipal Code Section 3-76 (Establishment of a Permit Parking District) through
Section 3-76.1 (Amending or Terminating a Permit Parking District).

Since the Parking and Traffic Commission has determined that permitted parking may not be
warranted in the area in question, ballots are mailed to all residences within the boundary of
the subject street.

If seventy-five percent (75%) or more of the returned ballots vote “approve” for the termination
of residential permit parking, then an ordinance amending the Residential Permit Parking
District will be submitted to the City Council for consideration. If approved, 3rd Avenue from
Manchester Boulevard to 90th Street within District 7C will not be subject to the Residential
Permit Parking District rules. Therefore, all vehicles can park on these streets without showing
a parking permit at all hours of the day, every day of the week. Additionally, the current
parking prohibitions for street sweeping will remain unchanged.

Using the enclosed ballot, please vote to approve or reject the termination of the residential
permit parking on 3rd Avenue from Manchester Boulevard to 90th Street within District 7C.
Please return the ballot to the City of Inglewood Public Works Department within the next
thirty (30) days. Only one vote per household will be accepted. If you have any questions,
please do not hesitate to get in touch with the Public Works Department, at (310) 412-5333.

RECOMMENDATION:
It is requested that the Parking and Traffic Commission review the information included in this
report and approve the resolution to terminate the Residential Permit Parking Program within
District 9 on 5th Avenue between 104th Street and 108th Street.

BACKGROUND:
In June 2020, the City Council adopted a Residential Permit Parking Program. The program is
enforced 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with two-hour parking Monday through Sunday, 8 a.m.
to 5 p.m. (Ordinance No. 20-09). The program was adopted to protect residential communities
more effectively and efficiently from non-resident vehicle intrusion.

On October 25, 2022, Public Works (PW) Department received a petition requesting the removal
of Residential Permit Parking for 5th Avenue between 104th Street and 108th Street. Fifteen
(15) valid signatures (one signature per residential unit) were submitted on the petition, resulting
in forty-one percent (41%) of all households on the block signing the petition in favor of removing
the permit parking restrictions.

On June 6, 2023, a notice was sent to the residents inviting them to the June Parking and Traffic
Commission meeting to express their views on the matter. The notice was sent to all residents
within the limits of the petition.

On June 28, 2023, the Parking and Traffic Commission held a public hearing on the issue of
terminating the Residential Permit Parking Program for 5th Avenue between 104th Street and
108th Street within District 9. The Public Works Department requested that the Parking and
Traffic Commission listen to public comments and provide direction on whether the petition
should go to a vote by the residents. As a result, all district commissioners voted to approve the
request to begin the voting process.

DISCUSSION:
On July 12, 2023, the Public Works Department mailed questionaries to each resident residing
in the boundary area of the petition and requested the questionnaires be returned within thirty
(30) calendar days. August 12, 2023 was the deadline for the City to accept responses to the
questionnaires. On August 15, 2023, the questionnaires were counted. Eleven (11) votes were
cast to approve the termination, while two (2) votes opposed the termination of the Residential
Permit Parking Program. Based on the number of votes received, eighty-five percent (85%) of

  NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
  Petition for Termination of Permit Parking in
  Residential Neighborhood
A petition has been submitted to the Inglewood Public Works Department requesting the termination of
residential permit parking within District 9 on 5th Avenue between 104th Street and 108th Street. Per
Sections 3-75 to 3-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code, this matter will be presented to the Inglewood
Parking and Traffic Commission at the time and place specified:

  Wednesday June 28, 2023 at 7:00 p.m.
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

This notice is being mailed to all addresses within the subject area. Any interested person may attend this
meeting and speak on this matter.

  Purpose of Public Hearing
The purpose of this public hearing is to give all residents of the subject area listed above an opportunity to
state their opinion of the subject matter.

The purpose of the Residential Permit Parking Program is to assure the availability to residents of some on-
street (curbside) parking spaces within a neighborhood where the patrons and/or employees of a nearby
commercial or industrial facility are otherwise using all available on-street parking spaces.

The Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission will therefore be considering if the availability of on-street
parking is severely impacted and if the termination of a residential permit parking within District 9 on 5th
Avenue between 104th Street and 108th Street would be warranted. If it is determined to be warranted,
ballots will be mailed to each household within the subject area.

If a Residential Permit Parking District is terminated, all residents and visitors in this neighborhood will not
be restricted from parking on the public streets at any time; including during special events. If you have any
questions regarding this matter, or wish to express an opinion but are unable to attend the public hearing,
please contact the Inglewood Public Works Department at (310) 412-5333.

Se ha presentado una petición al Departamento de Obras Públicas de Inglewood solicitando la cancelación
del permiso de estacionamiento residencial dentro del Distrito 9 en 5th Avenue entre 104th Street y 108th
Street. De acuerdo con las Secciones 3-75 a 3-79 del Código Municipal de Inglewood, este asunto se
presentará a la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico de Inglewood a la hora y lugar especificados:

  Miércoles 28 de Junio de 2023 a las 7:00p.m.
  En la Sala Comunitaria A en el Primer Piso
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

Este aviso se envía por correo a todas las direcciones dentro del área de asunto. Cualquier persona
interesada puede asistir a esta reunión y hablar sobre este tema.

  Propósito de la Audiencia Pública
El propósito de esta audiencia pública es dar a todos los residentes del área mencionada anteriormente la
oportunidad de expresar su opinión sobre el tema.

El propósito del Programa de Permisos de Estacionamiento Residencial es garantizar la disponibilidad para
los residentes de algunos espacios de estacionamiento en la calle (bordillo) dentro de un vecindario donde
los clientes y/o empleados de una instalación comercial o industrial cercana utilizan todos los espacios de
estacionamiento disponibles en la calle.

La Comisión de Tráfico y Estacionamiento de Inglewood, por lo tanto, considerará si la disponibilidad de
estacionamiento en la calle se ve gravemente afectada y si se justificaría la terminación de un permiso de
estacionamiento residencial dentro del Distrito 9 en la Quinta Avenida entre la Calle 104 y la Calle 108. Si
se determina que está justificado, las boletas se enviarán por correo a cada hogar dentro del área en
cuestión.

Si se rescinde un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial, no todos los residentes y visitantes
de este vecindario tendrán restricciones para estacionar en las calles públicas en cualquier momento;
incluso durante eventos especiales. Si tiene alguna pregunta sobre este asunto o desea expresar una
opinión pero no puede asistir a la audiencia pública, comuníquese con el Departamento de Obras Públicas
de Inglewood al (310) 412-5333.

Date:  Wednesday, July 12, 2023

To:  Residents of 5th Avenue

Subject:  Vote to Approve or Reject the termination of residential permit parking on
  5th Avenue from 104th Street to108th Street

The purpose of this letter is to allow residents the opportunity to vote on the removal of the
residential permit parking for 5th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street within District 9. By
voting "approve", this street will not be subject to the rules of a Residential Permit Parking
District. By voting "reject", this street will continue to have permitted parking and follow the
rules associated with it. The complete rules and procedures can be found in the Inglewood
Municipal Code Section 3-76 (Establishment of a Permit Parking District) through Section 3-
76.1 (Amending or Terminating a Permit Parking District).

Since the Parking and Traffic Commission has determined that permitted parking may not be
warranted in the area in question, ballots are mailed to all residences within the boundary of
the subject street.

If seventy-five percent (75%) or more of the returned ballots vote “approve” for the termination
of residential permit parking, then an ordinance amending the Residential Permit Parking
District will be submitted to the City Council for consideration. If approved, 5th Avenue from
104th Street to 108th Street within District 9 will not be subject to the Residential Permit
Parking District rules. Therefore, all vehicles can park on these streets without showing a
parking permit at all hours of the day, every day of the week. Additionally, the current parking
prohibitions for street sweeping will remain unchanged.

Using the enclosed ballot, please vote to approve or reject the termination of the residential
permit parking on 5th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street within District 9. Please return
the ballot to the City of Inglewood Public Works Department within thirty (30) days from the
date of this letter. Only one vote per household will be accepted. If you have any questions,
please do not hesitate to get in touch with the Public Works Department, at (310) 412-5333.

El propósito de esta carta es brindar a los residentes la oportunidad de votar sobre la
eliminación del permiso de estacionamiento residencial para la 3ra Avenida desde Manchester
Boulevard hasta la Calle 90 dentro del Distrito 7C. Al votar "aprobar", esta calle no estará sujeta
a las normas de un distrito de estacionamiento con permiso residencial. Al votar "rechazar",
esta calle seguirá teniendo estacionamiento permitido y seguirá las reglas asociadas con ella.
Las reglas y procedimientos completos se pueden encontrar en el Código Municipal de
Inglewood, Sección 3-76 (Establecimiento de un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso)
hasta la Sección 3-76.1 (Modificación o Terminación de un Distrito de Estacionamiento con
Permiso).

Dado que la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico ha determinado que es posible que no se
justifique el estacionamiento permitido en el área en cuestión, las boletas se envían por correo
a todas las residencias en la calle descrita anteriormente.

Si el setenta y cinco por ciento (75%) o más de las boletas devueltas votan “aprueban” la
terminación del permiso de estacionamiento residencial, se presentará una ordenanza que
modifica el Distrito de estacionamiento con permiso residencial al Concejo Municipal para su
consideración. Si se aprueba, 3rd Avenue desde Manchester Boulevard hasta 90th Street
dentro del Distrito 7C no estará sujeta a las reglas del Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso
Residencial. Por lo tanto, todos los vehículos pueden estacionar en estas calles sin mostrar un
permiso de estacionamiento a todas horas del día, todos los días de la semana. Además, las
prohibiciones de estacionamiento actuales para el barrido de calles se mantendrán sin
cambios.

Usando la boleta adjunta, vote para aprobar o rechazar la terminación del permiso residencial
de estacionamiento en 3rd Avenue desde Manchester Boulevard hasta 90th Street dentro del
Distrito 7C. Devuelva la boleta al Departamento de Obras Públicas de la Ciudad de Inglewood

pregunta, no dude en comunicarse con el Departamento de Obras Públicas al (310) 412-5333.
